notes: Meridian is an invented independent quarterly of cartography and territory (Issue 07, 'Uncertain Ground'), built as a static site: a homepage with masthead, original SVG cover chart, table of contents, editor's note and colophon, plus three full-length feature articles with standfirsts, margin notes, pull quotes, original SVG chart plates, footnotes and cross-linked related reading. Hand-written semantic HTML5 and CSS3 (grid layout, fluid type scale, spacing tokens); JavaScript is one small file used only for a reading-progress indicator and footnote quick-view popups, so every page remains fully readable and navigable without JS. All artwork is original inline SVG; there are no external requests, fonts, images or cookies. Article facts reference real events (Sandy Island 2012, the 1973/2022 Hans Island dispute, UNCLOS, Mandelbrot 1967, Seabed 2030) written from memory and deliberately hedged; bylines, editor and the publication itself are fictional. Verified in a real browser at desktop and mobile widths: navigation, anchors, skip link, focus styles and reduced-motion fallbacks checked; no console errors. Known limitations: display type relies on a system-font stack so letterforms vary slightly by platform; footnote popovers are a pointer/keyboard enhancement only and do not appear on touch. Model slug resolved from the runtime identifier 'account:zai-start-plan/GLM-5.3-Flash'; the environment also displayed another identifier (glm-5.4) and the final runtime value was used.
